A shorter, clearer booking flow for Supertails+ clinics. The booking sits on the landing page and finishes on one screen, so pet parents get the right care with less effort.

Booking a vet,

The problem

A fragmented booking journey hid the entry point, added unnecessary steps, and delayed key information.

Pet parents left before the wizard showed a clinic, a vet or a time.

Touchpoint

Booking was hidden

Three icons on the landing page. Nothing showed what booking involved.

Services

Other services stayed on the landing page

Grooming and vaccination had cards on the home page, but no way in from the booking flow.

Length

Five steps, announced up front

The stepper said “long” before showing a clinic, vet or time.

Choices

Defaults dressed as decisions

One pet, nearest clinic, best vet: three steps to confirm the obvious.

Price

The fee came last

Booking charges appeared on the overview, after all the effort.

Drop-off

Spread across every step

No single broken screen. Perceived length was the problem.

Five steps just to see a time?

1 of 5 · the old wizard, step by step

The solution

A booking you can see, finished on one screen.

The Clinic Services block on the landing page holds the whole booking: nearest clinic, vet, day and time. One details screen confirms the pet and the charges, then you pay.

  • Booking visible at the touchpoint

    Clinic, vet, day and time before any tap, on all three service tabs.

  • Defaults you can change

    Nearest clinic, best available vet and the next slot are pre-selected; pet, clinic and vet became edits, not steps.

  • Price and policy before payment

    The ₹49 fee, the 25% discount and the reschedule rule sit above the pay button.

  • Questions after the slot is safe

    Symptoms and grooming packages are asked after confirmation, and can be skipped.

Pick a time.
Pay. Done ♡

Key takeaways

A clearer path to healthier, happier pets.

By showing the booking instead of describing it, defaulting the routine choices and putting the price before the commitment, the flow feels as short as it is.

  • Fix the drop where it starts. The loss began at the touchpoint, so trimming the wizard would have optimised a flow most people never entered.
  • Defaults are decisions people don’t want to make. Pet, clinic and vet became edits, not steps.
  • Price is part of the design. The fee above the button removed the surprise at the end.
